lines: a16z general partners Anish Acharya and Jonathan Lai argue AI is collapsing the gap between a game idea and a playable prototype, opening game creation to non-specialists.

They say AI agents that operate tools like Blender and game engines let individuals cover gaps in code, art and design, and could cut big-studio production cycles from about a decade to 2-5 years, freeing studios to risk new IP.
In their view AI handles roughly the first 80% of production, but human intuition still decides the final 20% that makes a game engaging.
Lower costs make esoteric niches such as hyper-specific job simulators viable, and AI-driven decompilation and modding are reviving legacy games for modern platforms.

They see the next frontier as AI-native worlds that generate mechanics, quests and stories in real time, and suggest RTS-style game interfaces may be the most intuitive way for non-technical users to manage agent workflows.
title: The Next Era of Games: Mods, Agents, and Infinite Worlds
